ex.en: A good opportunity came up at work.
Let's go together next time.
I hope I get a chance to go to Korea.

fix.note: Use native numbers: 한 장, 두 장. For tickets, photos, paper.

ex.en: Two tickets, please.
Could you take a picture for me?
How many sheets of paper do you need?
They're my favorite author.
That writer's new book is out.
Wei is a webtoon artist.

fix.note: Passive 막히다: 길이 막혀요 = traffic is jammed.

ex.en: A car is blocking the road.
Water was leaking, so I blocked it with a towel.
Mom stopped us from going.

fix.note: More formal than 싸다; common in shops and ads.

ex.en: This store is cheaper.
The lunch menu here is reasonably priced.
I'm looking for an inexpensive hotel.
Try not to leave any food uneaten.
Please leave a message.
Save some cake for me too.

fix.en: as it is, the same, exactly

ex.en: Just leave it as it is.
You look just the same as 10 years ago.
I made it exactly by the recipe.

notes: Mostly clean. Fixed unnatural collocations (기회를 받다, 입을 막다 for coughing, 10년 전이랑 그대로), a vague note and three loose translations.
